title: Transforming Software Development with Generative AI: Empirical Insights on Collaboration and Workflow
extended_summary:
This paper examines how generative AI tools, especially ChatGPT and GitHub Copilot, are changing day-to-day work and collaboration in software development. The authors ask how software engineers and related knowledge workers use GenAI, what effects it has on their workflow, and how it may alter teamwork dynamics such as communication, feedback, and knowledge sharing.

The study is an exploratory multi-case qualitative study based on semi-structured interviews with 13 participants across software-related roles, including developers, data scientists, managers, designers, and technical leaders. The context is companies in Norway that had introduced GenAI into product development processes. Participants described uses such as getting unstuck, learning, creating boilerplate code, copywriting, working with existing code, and prompt engineering.

The main conclusion is that GenAI is perceived as increasing productivity, speed, motivation, and enjoyment by reducing repetitive work and supporting learning. At the same time, the paper argues that GenAI can reduce human-to-human knowledge sharing and pair programming, potentially disrupting the teamwork learning loop and weakening collaboration over time. The authors also note practical challenges such as confidentiality concerns, limited tool integration, outdated training data, and culturally biased outputs.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative exploratory multi-case interview study with 13 participants and no control group or quantitative causal design. It offers useful descriptive evidence about perceived effects, but credibility is limited by self-report and small sample size.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests potentially meaningful productivity and learning benefits, but the impact is based on qualitative perceptions rather than measured effect sizes. Overall impact is plausible but unclear in magnitude for general or priority populations.

interventions.use_case: Teacher- or worker-facing conversational use of ChatGPT/GPT-style systems for task support, including getting unstuck, interactive learning, prompt-based roleplay, boilerplate generation, code assistance, and feedback on writing.

finding.finding_summary: The study reports that 13 interviewees across developer, manager, designer, and data science roles used ChatGPT/Copilot daily or 'all the time' to speed up repetitive work, reduce interruptions, and complete tasks faster. Participants described substantial time savings on boilerplate writing and bids (e.g., one manager reported a bid that would normally take much longer was completed in 20 minutes), but this was qualitative rather than a controlled effect estimate.
finding.measure: Interview-reported productivity, time savings, and workflow efficiency

finding.finding_summary: The paper suggests GenAI supported learning, problem solving, and metacognitive 'rubber-ducking' by helping users articulate problems, explore alternatives, and learn faster. At the same time, it may reduce human collaboration and pair programming, potentially weakening team learning loops and knowledge sharing.
finding.measure: Interview themes on learning, collaboration, and problem-solving practices

finding.finding_summary: Participants reported increased motivation, fun, engagement, and work satisfaction from using GenAI, partly because it reduced tedious tasks and provided immediate feedback. The study is qualitative and does not report standardized scales or effect sizes.
finding.measure: Interview-reported motivation, enjoyment, and work satisfaction
